10.1002_adma.202507809: All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) utilizing solid electrolytes, which replace flammable liquid electrolytes, are regarded as one of the most promising prospective energy storage devices due to their inherent safety advantages and high energy density potential. As an emerging class of electrolytes for ASSBs, hydridoborates have attracted research interest because of their attractive material properties, including superior compatibility with metal anodes, low gravimetric density, and excellent solution processability. In this review, hydridoborate‐based solid electrolytes (SEs) for all‐solid‐state batteries, including boranuide‐based SEs, arachno ‐hydridoborate‐based SEs, nido ‐hydridoborate‐based SEs, closo ‐hydridoborate‐based SEs, and conjuncto ‐hydridoborate‐based SEs, are comprehensively summarized. Specifically, the strategies to improve ion conductivity, the ion conduction mechanism, and the performance of hydridoborate‐based SEs in ASSBs are discussed. Finally, the practical challenges for the application of hydridoborate SEs in ASSBs and the future development in the field are proposed. This review provides a detailed account of the advancements in hydridoborate‐based solid electrolytes, not only mapping the progress made in this field but also proposing an effective strategy for researchers to innovate efficiently to realize the practical applications of hydridoborate‐based SEs for the next generation of rechargeable batteries.
10.1021_acsenergylett.6c02372: Increased energy density and safety relative to conventional lithium (Li)-ion batteries motivate the development of solid-state batteries (SSBs). However, maintaining interface stability at the metal anode–solid electrolyte (SE) interface remains a critical challenge to achieving practical areal capacities, especially during stripping/discharge. Here, a mesoscale model informed by atomistic simulations is employed to examine void formation at the Li metal–SE interface during discharge/stripping. The model reveals how void-formation-driven interfacial contact loss behavior depends on the microstructural properties of the polycrystalline Li anode. In agreement with prior studies, Li microstructures with small grain sizes promote self-diffusion-induced void healing and generally exhibit better interfacial contact. We further show the effect of operating conditions, such as applied pressure, stripping current density, and temperature, on the stripping performance for different Li microstructures. Through this study, we shed light on the importance of taking microstructural features into account in predicting interfacial contact evolution during stripping of Li metal SSBs.
